source.label: Wizards Gen Con 2007 coverage, "Vintage Championship Top 8 Decklists" (Bill Stark)

notes.text: Swiss on Saturday 18 August; the Top 8 was played Sunday 19 August (coverage posts "Sunday, 11:23 a.m.: Vintage Championship Top 8" to "Sunday, 3:15 p.m.: Your 2007 Vintage Champion").

Unresolved: Wizards printed no bracket and no seeds. Menendian beat Ray Robillard in the quarterfinals, Vincent Forino in the semifinals and Rich Shay in the final (Menendian's report). Shay's semifinal opponent, who also finished 3-4, is not known, so the other five are all listed 5-8. mtgtop8 puts Robillard and Mattiuzzo at 3-4, which Menendian's report contradicts for Robillard; TCGplayer lists all six at 5th-8th.

source.label: Deckbox user lhc, set "Stephen Menendian - Gro-A-Tog" (2007 Champs)

notes.text: Wizards prints 56 main deck cards and no sideboard. The 4 Duress are added from the Deckbox copy (mtgtop8 agrees on Duress), and the sideboard, which no original source printed, is copied from Deckbox; mtgtop8's sideboard is the same. mtgtop8 has Mox Pearl where Wizards and Deckbox have Mox Ruby; Mox Ruby is kept.
Wizards' coverage prints "Steve Menendian". The Deckbox set above and the sources for his 2004 and 2011 Top 8s say Stephen; he is listed as Stephen in all three, so one person has one name.

Wizards prints the line "4 Duress" twice, for 64 cards; one is removed here, giving 60. The Deckbox copy and mtgtop8 both have 4 Duress. The extra line is almost certainly the 4 Duress missing from Menendian's list.

Wizards' coverage prints "Richard Shay". Menendian's report calls him Rich Shay, as the sources for his 2011, 2015, 2017 and 2018 Top 8s do; he is listed as Rich in all five, so one person has one name.
Semifinalist per Menendian's winner report ("Semifinals: Vincent Forino").
